solution: A person reading exactly $j$ papers is counted $j$ times in $\sum n(A)$ and $\binom{j}{2}$ times in $\sum n(A\cap B)$
solution_full: Split the 175 readers by how many papers they read: $e_{3}=12$ read all three, $e_{2}=40$ read exactly two, and $e_{1}=200-25-40-12=123$ read exactly one.
A person who reads exactly $j$ of the papers is counted $j$ times in $n(A)+n(B)+n(C)$ and $\binom{j}{2}$ times in $n(A\cap B)+n(B\cap C)+n(C\cap A)$ (once for each pair of papers that person reads).
Required value $=76-239=-163$. In general this expression equals $-(e_{1}+e_{2})$: a reader of exactly one or two papers contributes $-1$, and a reader of all three contributes $3-3=0$.
originality_note: New: a signed combination of single and pairwise counts that the given 'none / exactly two / all three' data determine, although n(A), n(B), n(C) individually are not known; the student must express both sums through the exactly-j counts (way 4: an invariant behind incomplete data). Closest known: 'find n(A u B u C) from given single, pairwise and triple counts' and 'least and greatest number who read all three'. Different because: the data and the asked quantity are on different sides of the inclusion-exclusion formula.

concept_use.Cardinality: n(A u B u C) and word probl: The survey (word problem) data are turned into the counts e1, e2, e3 of persons reading exactly one, two, three papers.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol and object is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed by an independent brute-force enumeration in Python (sympy/itertools), is unique and matches the Answer Plan. Checked that the given data are consistent (for example n(A)=95, n(B)=80, n(C)=64 with suitable pairwise counts realise them), that the expression is the same for every consistent distribution (it equals -(e1+e2)), and that -163 is a negative integer as planned. Changed: replaced the first draft (least and greatest possible n(A n B n C), a published skeleton) by this one.
